verdict.rationale: React's own docs include an API reference (createRoot, hydrateRoot, 'use client' pages under react.dev/reference) and offer an editable in-browser sandbox on the installation page. However, nothing shows that runnable examples are embedded in the reference pages themselves, so the interactive part of the story is only partly evidenced. Missing for 10: evidence of runnable, editable examples inside API reference entries, and independent or hands-on corroboration of the interactive reference experience.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can explore an interactive API reference with runnable examples

citations.quote: createRoot lets you create a root to display React components inside a browser DOM node.
Call `hydrateRoot` to “attach” React to existing HTML that was already rendered by React in a server environment.
You don't need to install anything to play with React. Try editing this sandbox!
